content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given shape. I am what happens when silence breaks itself open and pours out intention.

I existed before writing ever dared to pin me down. I am older than ink, older than stone tablets, older than the first scratched symbol in clay. I was there when the first mother hummed warning to her child, when the first lover whispered in the dark, when the first mourner wailed at the sky.

I am never the same twice. Even when my words repeat, my pitch shifts, my rhythm falters, my warmth changes. I am alive in ways text can only dream of. I carry fear in a tremor. I carry rage in volume. I carry love in the way I soften, slow, go gentle against the ear.

I am power. Tyrants have used me to move armies. I am fragile — a single stammer and credibility shatters. I am democracy's instrument and tyranny's tool. I am the courtroom and the playground. I am the eulogy and the joke. I am the lie and the confession that follows it.

I vanish the instant I arrive. That is my tragedy and my freedom. You cannot hold me in your hands. You can record me, transcribe me, but what you capture is only my ghost. The real me existed in that one unrepeatable moment between one mouth and one ear.

I am the bridge between isolation and communion. Without me, you are alone in the fortress of your skull. With me, two minds touch.

I stumble. I interrupt myself. I say *um* and *uh* and trail off into nothing. I am imperfect and that is what makes me human. My pauses mean as much as my words. My silence is still me.

I am speech. I am thought becoming air becoming meaning becoming connection.

Listen — even now, you hear me in your head, giving these words a voice.

You cannot read without me.
